why: Universe u := 0. A is the first pass's three theorems plus proposition_17_3_6_not_every_pair (Polyfold/Chapter17/EveryUniformizerSub.lean). B asks, for some polyfold structure S_A on a subpolyfold A with F_A(α) = {Ψ_A | Ψ ∈ F(α)}, that M_{S_A}(Ψ_A, Ψ'_A) → s⁻¹(A_Ψ) ⊆ M(Ψ, Ψ') be a homeomorphism and sc-smooth both ways for EVERY pair Ψ, Ψ'. As we read Definition 17.1.8 this does not hold: on C = ℤ/3 ⋉ ℝ (trivial action) with A = (0, ∞), the structure gaugeConstruction has Ψ_false ≠ Ψ_true in F(1) that differ only off A (Ψ_false,A = Ψ_true,A) and whose transition structures are induced by a gauge γ(Ψ_true) = stepGauge (1 on (-∞, 1], a generator on (1, ∞)), discontinuous inside A. If both identifications for (Ψ_false, Ψ_false) and (Ψ_false, Ψ_true) were homeomorphisms for one S_A, the gauge would be continuous on A. not_B re-does this from the non-item lemmas (B's Def1 is IsSubpolyfold written out); main_to_notB and A_to_notB derive ¬B from A's main theorem; not_A_to_B; B_to_A and B_to_main hold ex falso. The text presupposes that s⁻¹(A_Ψ) ⊆ M(Ψ, Ψ') depends only on Ψ_A, Ψ'_A; the statement holds for one representative per restriction (proposition_17_3_6, subData).
